html:
Leabua Jonathan was the first prime minister of Lesotho, leading it from independence on 4 October 1966 until he was overthrown in 1986.

A chief and former mine worker, he led the Basotho National Party, backed by the Catholic Church and at first by South Africa, to a narrow victory in 1965. When he seemed to be losing the 1970 election, he cancelled it, suspended the constitution and ruled by decree, sending King Moshoeshoe II into exile for a time.

He later turned against apartheid and let the ANC shelter in Lesotho. South Africa raided Maseru in 1982 and in 1986 blockaded the border, and the army removed him. The country stayed bound to its giant neighbour, as the protectorate years and migrant work had made it.
